messages:
Erin: seeing a sharp spike of 503s from hosted inference around 11:12 UTC. Upstream inference workers in gpu-pool-4 are restarting frequently.
Sam: confirmed on dashboards — 5xx rate jumped to ~12% and p95 latency doubled. Is this toolcall-related or an embed storm?
Erin: it's correlated with authenticated toolcall endpoints. Logs show repeated OOMs followed by a segfault in the runtime: 
```log
[11:12:03] worker-23 ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[11:12:03] worker-23 FATAL: signal 11 (segfault) at runtime.c:482
[11:12:04] k8s: container restartCount=1
```
Priyanka: CS reports multiple customers (Acme, EchoApps) hit timeouts and streaming connections dropped. They're escalating.
cs-team: Acme opened ticket #12345 — saw 503s for ~3 minutes, lots of aborted streams on their side.
Darren: any kube events or preemption? Could be spot preemptions or OOM kills.
Erin: kube events show container exits with no preemption label. nvml logs indicate memory pressure then device reset on worker-23. No system OOM on host.
Sam: quick mitigation: enable route fallback to a smaller model variant for affected customers and roll back last canary if necessary. @infra-bot can you apply fallback for acme-prod?
infra-bot: fallback-route applied to route 'acme-prod' -> 'redwood-small' at 11:15:02 UTC (route-id route-7f3a).
Priyanka: can we fetch core or heap dumps? Any coredump captured?
Erin: no corefile present; process exited with SIGSEGV and k8s cleaned the pod. We pulled GPU memory timeline and logs. Snippet: 
```bash
curl -sS http://logs.internal/worker/worker-23 | jq '.gpu_memory_samples' | tail -n 20
# shows a rapid spike from ~2GB -> ~12GB in under 400ms before crash
```
Darren: sounds like kv-prefetch + a large toolcall context pushed memory over the canary quant profile. We did a quant swap to quantized-v2 in the canary at ~11:10, right?
Erin: yes — we pushed quantized-v2 to a small canary pool at 11:10 and that canary included some heavy-auth routes (mistake). Canary rollback initiated at 11:16.
Sam: reproducible checklist for QA: 1) set model to quantized-v2 on a canary pool; 2) issue concurrent authenticated toolcall requests with large context (>50k tokens); 3) monitor GPU memory and container exit. Priyanka, can you own repro run and post artifacts?
Priyanka: running a controlled blast now. Will capture nvml timelines, logs, and a flamegraph. I'll upload a gist after run.
cs-team: told Acme support we have temporary fallback active and are rolling back the canary. They're asking for ETA to resolution.
Darren: mitigation status: fallback applied and rollback in progress. If rollback stabilizes by 11:30 we'll confirm with CS. If not, plan B is to throttle toolcall concurrency for heavy routes and/or scale the pool by +25%.
infra-bot: rollback job started: job-id rb-20231105-11:17 (status: in_progress).
Erin: follow-ups: 1) enable coredump capture on SIGSEGV for inference runners, 2) collect full nvml logs for workers in gpu-pool-4, 3) add memory guardrail to canary policy to exclude heavy-auth routes, 4) create a short postmortem draft.
Sam: also add a span/tag in traces for 'toolcall_large_ctx' to make queries easier.
Priyanka: repro complete — uploaded artifacts: https://gist.github.com/priyanka/repro-oom-171888 (includes nvml timeline, logs, and flamegraph). Initial notes: crash reproduces when context > ~48k tokens + simultaneous prefetch.
cs-team: updated Acme with rollback and fallback status; they requested notification once full rollback validated.
Darren: ack. I'll monitor the pool, follow up in 15m, and draft a blameless postmortem. If rollback doesn't stabilize, I'll enact concurrency throttles and open an urgency for infra to patch quant runtime memory accounting.
Erin: thanks — assigning oncall to follow for 2 hours: @Darren. :thumbsup:
Sam: adding runbook note and action items to the incident board.
